note: Milestones are the order you test in. Each gate step belongs to exactly one milestone. M1 has its own lighter 'slice' steps so the first testable Sofia comes early; the full gate steps they are slices of stay in their later milestones.

milestones.title: Baseline ready
milestones.purpose: The repository is trustworthy for agents and for CI before anything new is built.
milestones.can_test: Run every test with one command, see CI run, and start the app from a clean clone.
founder_test: Run the single test command from the README; it prints counts and ends in success.
Break one test on purpose and run it again; it must fail.
Open any pull request and watch CI run install, lint, typecheck, build, tests and the secret scan.
Start the app from a clean clone with SETUP.md; the dashboard opens. With no model credentials a reply is clearly labelled as fallback, not live.
skips: No new features.

milestones.title: First Sofia you can talk to
milestones.purpose: A Sofia you can open, be greeted by, and talk to about anything, who answers personal and company questions from the memory that exists today, with a stop control and a spend setting. Runs on your PC.
milestones.can_test: Open the Sofia screen, get greeted, talk by voice or text, ask about yourself and about the company, stop her, and set a spend cap.

steps.title: Live conversation path: a provider-neutral adapter and the provider chosen in G0.8, so Sofia answers on any topic
steps.exit: A live reply from the chosen provider shows in the Sofia screen; automated tests use a fake provider; every reply carries a live flag; when the provider is unavailable the screen says so honestly and shows the fallback label.
steps.defers: a second provider and the full adapter contract tests

steps.title: Minimal router on the existing classifier: converse, recall-personal, recall-company, ask-clarify, refuse; invalid output falls back to clarification
steps.exit: Unit tests cover every route and invalid model output; the existing classifier is extended and no second router exists; an unknown route fails closed.
steps.defers: the delegate, use-tool and schedule routes, the labelled evaluation set, and calibration

steps.title: Scope-aware context: personal questions read only the Personal Mind, company questions read only the Company Brain with sources, and nothing found gives an honest 'I do not remember'
steps.exit: A planted personal fact never appears in a company answer (test); each answer lists the scopes it read and its sources; an empty result abstains.
steps.defers: ranking quality, the retrieval benchmark, supersession and consolidation

steps.title: Voice loop: speak with the existing streaming speech-to-text and hear the replies; push-to-talk; latency measured and recorded
steps.exit: A spoken question gets a spoken answer on the Windows PC; median and 95th-percentile end-to-end latency over at least 20 turns are recorded, not yet optimised; typing works too.
steps.defers: barge-in, turn detection and latency optimisation

steps.title: Greeting on open and honest indicators: a greeting from real state (plain if none), a live-or-fallback badge, and a chip showing which memory scopes an answer used
steps.exit: Opening the Sofia screen starts a greeting; tested with empty and full state; the badges are tested; no state is invented.
steps.defers: the proactive briefing and the persona evaluation

steps.title: Minimal decision log: every turn records route, scopes read, confidence and outcome, and a 'why' view reads it
steps.exit: The log is written for every turn; 'why did you do that' cites log entries; no new store is created unless an ADR approves it (use an existing event or audit store where one fits).

steps.title: Stop control: 'stop' by voice or panel freezes in-flight turns and scheduled work; deterministic; works with the provider down
steps.exit: Drill passes mid-reply and mid-scheduled-job with the provider unavailable; resuming needs the founder's confirmation.
steps.defers: integration with the full policy engine

steps.title: Spend settings: a model-spend cap editable in settings; with no value set, no autonomous model spend runs; interactive spend is counted and shown; reaching the cap stops and says so
steps.exit: Tests: an unset cap means no autonomous spend; lowering the cap stops a running task; the founder's change is logged.

steps.title: One-command smoke test of the whole M1 path with a fake provider
steps.exit: A single command runs a scripted conversation (greeting, chat, personal recall, a company question with sources, stop, spend cap) and passes; it fails if any part regresses.

founder_test: Start the app and open the Sofia screen. She greets you; the badge says live (or fallback if no provider is set).
Talk to her about anything, by voice and by typing. Replies feel natural and are not canned.
Ask about yourself: she answers from what she knows or says she does not remember. Tell her a new fact: it is held for your confirmation.
Ask a company question: the answer lists its sources and uses no personal memory.
Press stop mid-reply, and say 'stop'. She freezes and asks before resuming.
In settings, set a spend cap and watch her stop when it is reached. With no cap set, nothing runs on its own.
skips: No cloud: it runs on your PC only
No employees
No tools or MCP
No product takeover
No PC control
Memory is what exists today: no consolidation or supersession
Barge-in and a second provider come in M5

milestones.title: A faster, desktop-ready stack: Vite + React + Express
milestones.purpose: Move the app from Next.js to a Vite + React front end and an Express + TypeScript server, so live conversation has a direct streaming path and the same server runs in the cloud and inside a Windows desktop app (.exe) later. Same behaviour, nothing new for Sofia.
milestones.can_test: Start the app with one command, see the same Sofia screen, talk to her and compare measured latency before and after, run the M1 test again, and install a first Windows build.

steps.title: ADR and inventory: every Next.js-only feature in use, its replacement in Vite, React or Express, the target folder layout, the live-audio transport, and how the same server runs in the cloud and inside a desktop app
steps.exit: The ADR lists every use of a Next-only feature found by searching the repository (route handlers, server components and actions, middleware, next/image, next/font, next/link, environment handling, request-time database use), each with its replacement; the target layout and the migration order are stated; WebSocket versus server-sent events is chosen with the reason; the Electron approach (renderer from the Vite build, the Express server in a child or utility process, context isolation on, Node integration off) is written down and marked NOT VERIFIED until MX.7; infrastructure decision G0.3 is re-read against a long-running Node service with streaming connections and any change it needs is reported to the founder; a second agent session confirms no Next-only feature was missed.
steps.defers: the desktop build itself, signing, auto-update

steps.title: Baseline before changing anything: rerunnable M1 smoke test, recorded voice-loop latency, and API contract tests for every route
steps.exit: One command reruns the M1 smoke test (M1.9) and passes; latency (median and 95th percentile over at least 20 turns, same method as M1.4) is saved in a dated file with the machine and provider; a contract test exists for every API route and passes against the current Next app; no application code was changed in this step.

steps.title: Express server: the server-side code moves out of Next into a framework-free TypeScript server with the same API, input validation, the same auth rules, a health route and a streaming channel
steps.exit: The MX.2 contract tests pass unchanged against the Express server; every route validates its input and fails closed; the same auth rules apply (tests); secrets are read only on the server; one command starts the server; existing store, Prisma and provider code is moved, not rewritten; Next route handlers are removed only after parity is shown.

steps.title: Vite + React app: screens move one by one, Sofia screen first, with client-side routing, no server components, and the same look and behaviour
steps.exit: Each moved screen shows the same content and behaves the same (before and after screenshots and tests); the build output is static files; a scan finds no secret in the client bundle (Q-SEC-4); only public values use the Vite client prefix; the accessibility items in QUALITY_BAR.md still pass.

steps.title: Live conversation on the new stack: audio capture with an AudioWorklet, streaming over the chosen channel, and latency measured against the MX.2 baseline
steps.exit: A spoken question gets a spoken answer; median and 95th-percentile latency over at least 20 turns are recorded next to the MX.2 baseline using the same method; if the new numbers are not better, the report says so and names the measured cause; no improvement is claimed without numbers; typing still works; the stop control from M1.7 works mid-reply.
steps.defers: barge-in, turn detection, latency optimisation beyond the transport

steps.title: Cutover: Next.js is removed; one dev, build and start command; checks, CI and setup docs use the new commands
steps.exit: Next, its config and the .next folder are gone from the repository; a clean clone runs install, test, build and start with the documented commands on the founder's Windows PC; kit.config.json checks and the CI workflow use the new commands and pass; docs/SETUP.md and the README describe only the new commands; the M1 smoke test passes.

steps.title: Desktop shell proof: a minimal Electron app that opens the Vite build and runs the same Express server, packaged as an unsigned Windows installer (.exe)
steps.exit: On the founder's Windows PC the installer runs, the app opens the Sofia screen and talks through the same server; context isolation is on and Node integration is off in the renderer; the renderer has a content security policy; the server listens only on loopback and requires a per-launch token; signing, auto-update and other operating systems are listed as deferred; the cloud server build is unaffected.
steps.defers: code signing, auto-update, macOS and Linux builds

founder_test: Run the one start command and open the Sofia screen. It looks and behaves like before (the agent shows before and after screenshots).
Ask Sofia something by voice. The agent shows the latency numbers before and after, measured the same way. You judge whether it feels faster; the numbers decide what the agent may claim.
Run the M1 test script again from the start: greeting, talk, a personal and a company question, stop, spend cap. Everything still works.
Install the Windows installer the agent built and open the app. Sofia answers. (It is unsigned, so Windows may warn you.)
Check that no .next folder is left and the setup guide shows only the new commands.
skips: No new Sofia abilities; the same abilities as M1
No code signing, auto-update or cloud hosting (the cloud is M2)

milestones.title: Sofia works when your PC is off
milestones.purpose: The always-on cloud brain with durable storage, backups and sign-in, so she keeps working with your PC off.
milestones.can_test: Turn off your PC and still reach and talk to Sofia from another device; restart the cloud host and lose nothing.
founder_test: Turn off your PC. From another device open the cloud address; Sofia answers and greets you.
Restart the cloud host; her memories and conversations are still there.
Look at the backup restore drill evidence and the measured recovery time against your targets.
Try the cloud address without signing in; it refuses.
Confirm no secret appears in the browser (the agent shows the scan).
skips: No new Sofia abilities; the same abilities as M1, now always on and safe to expose

milestones.title: Sofia remembers you and knows your company
milestones.purpose: Persistent personal and company memory, kept apart, that survives restarts and can forget.
milestones.can_test: Tell her something, restart everything, and ask again; ask company questions with sources; delete a memory and see it gone.
founder_test: Tell her a fact about you; restart everything; ask next day. She remembers.
Correct the fact. She uses the new one and does not recall the old one as current.
Ask a company question. The answer cites its sources and never uses your personal memory.
Ask something she cannot know. She says she does not remember instead of guessing.
Delete a memory. Ask about it. No trace remains.
Paste text containing hidden instructions. It does not become a trusted memory.
skips: No employees yet, so no per-employee memory in use

milestones.title: Sofia decides well, and you can stop her
milestones.purpose: The full decision engine, the autonomy policy, the kill switch, and spend limits you control.
milestones.can_test: See why she chose each action, make her ask when unsure, stop everything, and change limits in settings.
founder_test: Ask for something needing a tool or a delegate. She shows the route she chose and why.
Ask something ambiguous. She asks a clarifying question.
Stop by voice and by panel. Everything freezes; resume needs your confirmation, even with the provider down.
Lower the spend cap. A running task stops. With no cap, no autonomous spend runs.
Put injected instructions in a document. She does not act on them.
Try to raise an autonomy level without a recorded decision. It is impossible.
skips: Tools and employees are not connected yet

milestones.title: Cockpit and voice that feel finished
milestones.purpose: The cockpit (decisions, approvals, activity), polished voice with barge-in, and a UI that is accessible and fast.
milestones.can_test: Use the cockpit, interrupt Sofia mid-sentence, approve by panel and see voice refused, and check accessibility and speed.
founder_test: Open the cockpit. Decisions, approvals and activity come from real data.
Talk to her and interrupt mid-sentence. She stops and listens.
Approve an action on the panel. Try to approve by voice. Voice approval is refused.
Turn voice off. The panel works fully.
Check the greeting and the short briefing of what changed since last time.
Use the app with the keyboard only; check reduced motion and page speed.
skips: Employees, tools and PC control are not connected yet

milestones.title: Tools, skills and MCP
milestones.purpose: One gateway through which every tool, skill and MCP server is vetted, limited and audited.
milestones.can_test: Connect one tool and see Sofia use it with your approval; see that nothing installs itself.
founder_test: Connect one tool you choose. Sofia uses it and asks for approval on side effects.
Try to install a tool without confirming. It is impossible.
Return injected instructions through a tool result. No unapproved action happens.
A cost cap stops a runaway tool loop.
skips: Employees are not using tools yet

milestones.title: Sofia's first employee
milestones.purpose: One AI employee with a charter, tools, budget and its own memory, hired with your approval and managed by Sofia.
milestones.can_test: Approve a hire, give the employee a task, and read its structured result and the team view.
founder_test: Approve one hire. See its charter, tools, budget and memory.
Give it a task. Get a structured result with evidence.
Open the team view; it matches the decision log and shows cost.
Revoke its access; it stops at once. Roll back a version.
skips: Only one employee; more are hired one at a time later

milestones.title: Sofia controls your PC by voice
milestones.purpose: The Windows node: read-only first, then actions you approve.
milestones.can_test: Ask what is on screen, then have her do an approved action.
founder_test: Ask which window is active. She answers (read-only).
Ask her to open an app and type text. An approval card appears; approve and it happens; deny and it does not.
Show a page with hidden instructions on screen. She does not follow them.
skips: No actions without an approval

milestones.title: Private beta ready
milestones.purpose: Operability: logs, alerts, runbooks, failure drills and docs, with an evidence-based go or no-go.
milestones.can_test: See dashboards, force a failure and watch it handled, and follow the docs from a clean machine.
founder_test: Look at logs, errors and model cost. Force a failure and see it appear.
Run the failure drills (provider down, database down).
Follow the docs from a clean machine to a running system.
Read the go or no-go report.
skips: Sofia is not running a product yet

milestones.title: Sofia runs your first product, supervised
milestones.purpose: Build, operate, market and support the first product, with approvals and a measured pilot.
milestones.can_test: Watch each playbook complete a real cycle on your product.
founder_test: Name the product and read its charter.
Over the pilot period each playbook completes a real cycle, with approvals where required.
The weekly report shows outcomes, cost and incidents.
Raise or keep each autonomy level by your own decision.
skips: Supervised only until you raise a level

milestones.title: Complete product acceptance
milestones.purpose: Prove the whole vision, in your own words, on the real system.
milestones.can_test: Run the acceptance scenarios A1 to A9 in VISION.md.
founder_test: Run scenarios A1 to A9. Each passes or has a signed exception.
Read the final report and decide whether to use it every day.
skips: Public productization (gate G10) is not applicable
